title: The Powers Above and Three Righteous Men
english: Fragments from the Catenae on Ezekiel.

“And four wings for each one” (Ezekiel 1:6). For in a sense the rational powers on high always stand: they do not sink down toward baser things, but speed along the straight and blameless path of the life that befits them.

“And they shall be on the mountains like doves” (Ezekiel 7:16). These are the blessed disciples. For they went about all the earth under heaven, speaking the mystery of Christ (Colossians 4:3), and they had it as their song and their lyre.

“And if these three men, Noah and Daniel and Job, are in its midst” (Ezekiel 14:14). Since I think we must not leave the prophet’s words unexamined, come, let us say why it is that, when Noah and Job and Daniel were already dead (and perhaps even Daniel himself), he says that they will be saved by their own righteousness (Ezekiel 14:14), even though all the rest of the land, against which the sentence of death might be pronounced, is being destroyed.
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 70, Fragmenta in Ezechielem (Greek), via the Khazarzar transcription.
Heading: the Latin edition headings 'Fragmenta in Ezechielem / FRAGMENTA EX CATENIS IN EZECHIELEM' are given in English as one heading line.
Catena folio references (Cat. Ezech. f. 12b; Cat. 18b; Cat. f. 203b) and the PG column number 70.1460 are dropped from the reading text.
νοεραὶ καὶ ἄνω δυνάμεις: 'the rational powers on high', Cyril's usual term for the angelic orders; 'intellectual' rejected as misleading in modern English.

οὐκ ὀκλάζουσαι: literally 'not bending the knee' or 'not crouching'; rendered 'do not sink down'. The comment on standing may also look to the straight legs of Ezekiel 1:7, but only 1:6 is quoted, so no reference is added for 1:7.
Οἱ μακάριοι μαθηταί stands without a verb; 'These are the blessed disciples' supplies only the copula that identifies the doves.
πᾶσαν ὑπ' οὐρανόν: 'all the earth under heaven'; a possible echo of Colossians 1:23 (ἐν πάσῃ κτίσει τῇ ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν) is left uncited.

Νῶε καὶ Ἰὼβ καὶ Δανιὴλ τεθνεώτων ἤδη, τάχα δέ που καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Δανιήλ: the printed text names Daniel in the list of the dead and then adds 'and perhaps even Daniel himself'. Rendered as printed, with the second phrase in parentheses; the sense is probably that Noah and Job were long dead and Daniel perhaps also by Ezekiel's time. No emendation made.
ἡ τοῦ θανάτου ψῆφος: 'the sentence of death'; ψῆφος is a judicial vote or verdict.
The section ends at a full stop; Cyril's answer begins in the next section, 'Noah, Daniel, Job, and the Cedar'.
